seal.statement: test-output/ reached 40 GB by 2026-09-17, with single files up to 2.1 GB, although scripts/prune-test-output.js has existed since March with a careful twelve-category policy. The same thing happened in July - that commit reads 'test-output/ reached 6.7GB because the pruner existed but was never invoked' - and its fix wired the pruner into the rolling-restart stat-gate only, which is not the routine path, so the accumulation simply resumed. Retention now runs on the routine path: every publish applies the stat-gate's own history-safe policy (7 days, floors of 24 reports and playbacks, above the harness's 20-report comparison window) after the push and the receipt, bounded and never raised. Making it routine exposed a flaw that the occasional manual run had hidden: a top-level directory's age was its own inode mtime, which moves only when an entry is added or removed, so a directory whose files are rewritten in place looked old while its contents were fresh. Measured against the real checkout on 2026-09-18: six directories the old rule would have deleted on the first routine run held files written in the last four days (tlc on 09-14, five harness fixture directories on 09-17), and test-output/analysis - the generated import graph npm test reads - survived only because its inode happened to be recent. Age is now the newest content, measured in the walk that already sizes each entry. The parents of registered git worktrees (push-gate-worktrees, publish-worktrees) are reserved, because an rm -rf there leaves a worktree registered with its directory gone. The first routine run on this checkout removes 290 MB: 2872 stale report files, 19 stale top-level directories and 664 .tap results for tests not run in a week.

text: every publish runs the existing pruner after the push and the receipt, with the stat-gate's history-safe policy (7 days, floors of 24), bounded at 5 minutes and never raised; the pruner judges a directory's age by its newest content (measured in the walk that already sizes it) instead of the inode mtime, and reserves the parents of registered git worktrees. Measured on the real checkout: the first routine run removes 290 MB, and six directories the old age rule would have deleted hold files written in the last four days. The publisher's call site is witnessed end to end in the tap suite (an ordered record of gate, push, receipt, prune) and by mutation; the receipt set uses the node:test witnesses because --test-name-pattern cannot select a tap test

round 1 REJECT (1 blocking): the constraint history-window-preserved was false on the real checkout. loadHistoricalReports in test/distributed/run.js takes the 20 newest *.report.json that carry a scenarios array; test-output/reports held 213 of them, all marked for deletion, because the 24-report floor counts every json and was spent entirely on model reports (TLC/Alloy, fixed names, rewritten in place on every corpus run, no scenarios). The statement's and the publisher comment's claim that retention can never degrade a baseline comparison was therefore untrue, and this change makes that deletion routine. Verified sound: the new top-level age rule (new plan a strict subset of the old one on the same fixture), the worktree-parent reservation (no registered worktree lives under test-output), the publisher wiring (after the push and the receipt, from the caller's root, cannot change the exit status or touch the publish receipt), symlink handling (the walk never follows a link out of the tree and never loops), and 0.47 s for a dry run over 5.4 GB. Non-blocking: N1 directory dates below the top level ignored; N2 some new behaviour unwitnessed; N3 one unmeasurable entry aborts all retention, so retention would silently stop; N4 a future-dated file pins its tree; N5 pruning live .tap results loses the lane planner's longest-first history; N6 analysis safe only while written; N7 storage-load (the only local copy of the 24 h soak) ages out around 09-22; N8 stale worktree children never cleaned; N9 a timeout reports no reason; N10 statement counts slightly off; N11 the call site witnessed only in the tap suite.

round 1 repair. B1: the newest harness reports - *.report.json files carrying a scenarios array, exactly what the harness history reads - are pinned by kind through the existing pinnedNames path, parsing newest first only until the floor is met; on the real checkout 24 harness reports now survive and none of the current 20-report window is deleted, where all 213 were marked before. Also taken: N1 directory dates anywhere in the tree count as activity; N3 an entry that cannot be measured (dangling link, unreadable directory, a file gone mid-walk) is kept and the prune proceeds, in both walks and every listing stat; N4 a future-dated file does not count as freshness at all (my first version clamped it to now, which would have kept its tree forever - caught before review); N5 a .tap result whose test file still exists is kept, so only results of deleted tests age out (526 orphaned results, 0 MB, instead of 664 live ones); N9 a timed-out prune reports the spawn error or signal; N10 the statement's figures are corrected. Five new witnesses, each red when its fix is reverted. N6 is covered by N1 plus the newest-content rule; N7 (storage-load) is an owner decision and is surfaced, not coded; N8 is recorded as a follow-up.

Round 2 reject. B1 (harness history) fixed and confirmed on the real checkout: 24 scenario reports kept, the 20-report window identical before and after, dry run 3430 entries / 228 MB in 0.54 s. Blocking B2: measureEntry read the clock once at the start of the walk and treated any later mtime as no freshness, so a file appended during the walk (5/5 runs with a 2 ms appender under a 40,000-file old tree) or dated a few seconds ahead made a live tree look abandoned and deleted it - breaking live-output-kept. Non-blocking: the future rule was not applied to top-level entries, directory dates or reports; unmeasurable entries were kept silently; pathExists rethrew ENOTDIR/EACCES in the live .tap check and fs.rm EACCES stopped every later delete, both contrary to retention-never-silently-stops; mutations (i) direct-children-only freshness, (j) playback folder age by content, (p) the timeout message and (r) .tap folder-read tolerance stayed green; pruneTestOutput at cyclomatic 18.

Round-2 repairs. Every modification date passes one rule, evidenceOfUse, judged against the clock when that date is read with a one-day future tolerance: a date past it counts for nothing, anything else counts as use - so a file written during the walk or by a writer seconds ahead keeps its tree, and a 2099 date still pins nothing; statOrFresh applies the same rule, so top-level entries, directory dates and reports agree. Listing reads through readdirOrNothing: an absent directory is empty, any other failure lists nothing and is recorded; measureEntry and statOrFresh record what they could not measure; the summary line the publisher prints ends with how many were kept unmeasured and how many deletes failed, and the lines after name them. deleteEntries attempts every entry and records failures instead of stopping later categories. The live .tap check asks mayExist: only ENOENT or ENOTDIR is absence, anything else keeps the result. pruneFailureReason moved out of pruneTestOutput. Tests: a tree written 5 s ahead is kept; far-future top-level file, directory date and report all age out; deep activity with every directory above it old; a playback folder by content; an unreadable subtree and an unreadable .tap folder kept, named, the rest pruned; a failed delete reported while a later category still prunes; a result through a file dropped and an unverifiable one kept; timeout and signal reasons. 13 mutations, all red. Real-checkout dry run unchanged: 3430 entries, 228 MB, nothing unmeasured.

Round 3 approve. B2 fixed: a 40,000-file old tree with a 2 ms appender kept 8/8 (round 2 deleted it 5/5) while an identical tree without a writer was deleted 8/8; atomic-rename and create/delete churn kept; 3 s and 23 h ahead kept, 25 h ahead and 2099 are no freshness for inner files, top-level files, a directory's own date and reports. One fixture with an unreadable subtree, an undeletable folder, a dangling link, an ENOTDIR and an EACCES test path and an unreadable .tap folder exits 0 with 'Deleted 4 ... 1 could not be deleted. 3 kept because they could not be measured.', names each, and still removes the stale siblings. Real checkout dry run 0.57 s, 3430 entries / 228 MB path-for-path identical to round 2, nothing unmeasured. 33 mutations all red, including the round-2 survivors and the exact round-2 bug (4 receipts red). Harness 14/14, probe done, complexity 1819/1819 and cognitive 160/160. Non-blocking: churn can mark an entry unmeasured spuriously (kept safely); an EACCES-kept .tap result is not listed as unmeasured; orphan result folders stay empty; permission tests skip as root; the pruner is 820 lines (the 800-line ratchet covers src only); N7 soak copy, N8 stale worktree children, test-output/report.json outside the pin and mtime-versus-timestamp pin order remain open.
